headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Pipecat can send conversation content to external APIs while Replit Agent has broad filesystem and shell access.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pipecat ingests text, audio, video, and shared-bus conversation state, so attacker-controlled content can enter its outputs. Replit Agent can read workspace files and act on them, creating a plausible bridge if Pipecat output is written into the Repl. No direct provenance or isolation is documented for the pair, so the interaction is inferred and escalated above low.
conditions: IF Pipecat outputs are written into Replit workspace files or prompts, THEN injected instructions can reach Replit Agent.
IF Replit Agent treats Pipecat-generated text as authoritative, THEN prompt injection can steer tool use.
mitigations: Keep Pipecat outputs out of files Replit Agent reads.
Add a manual review step before any Pipecat text is pasted into Replit prompts.
Prefix imported content as untrusted data in prompts.
Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and filtering between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Pipecat touches audio, video, images, text, and conversation state and has allowlisted network egress to many third-party APIs. Replit Agent can read/write the Repl filesystem and handles secrets. If shared workspace data includes sensitive material, Pipecat can transmit it externally while Replit can access it locally, creating a realistic exfiltration path with broad blast radius.
conditions: IF sensitive audio, text, or secrets are placed in a shared workspace, THEN both agents can access them through different channels.
IF Pipecat is configured to call external STT/LLM/TTS services, THEN content may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in any shared workspace used by both agents.
Restrict Pipecat to non-sensitive test data.
Disable or narrow external service integrations in Pipecat.
Store Replit secrets only in the secrets store, not files.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention and egress allowlists per data class.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Pipecat supports shared-bus session state and multiple instances, while Replit Agent has write_filesystem, modify_git_state, and spawn_subprocesses. If both operate on the same workspace or repo, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide without documented locking. The pairwise conflict is plausible by default in a shared Repl-style workflow, so severity is high.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or directory, THEN concurrent edits can overwrite each other.
IF Replit Agent commits while Pipecat-generated artifacts are still changing, THEN git state can become inconsistent.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate directory.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Avoid concurrent git operations.
Use explicit file locks for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking and merge arbitration.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pipecat can generate conversation state and content that Replit Agent may treat as input for code or deployment changes. Replit Agent has shell and git authority, so a mistaken Pipecat output can cascade into incorrect edits or actions. There is no documented verification layer between them, but the blast radius is bounded by the Repl workspace, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Replit Agent uses Pipecat output as instructions or facts without verification, THEN errors can propagate into code or deployments.
IF Pipecat produces hallucinated or stale content, THEN Replit Agent may act on it.
mitigations: Require human review before shell or git actions.
Separate factual summaries from executable instructions.
Ask Replit Agent to verify Pipecat outputs against source files.
Limit Pipecat to drafting, not execution.
requires-engineering: add automated validation gates before commits or deployments.

E_compliance.rationale: Pipecat can route audio, video, images, and text to third-party services via network egress, while Replit Agent handles secrets and workspace files in a cloud Repl. If regulated data such as EU PII or secrets enters the pair, residency and retention obligations may diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is processed by Pipecat and stored in a Replit workspace, THEN retention and residency obligations may diverge.
IF the operator routes EU PII or PHI through external Pipecat services, THEN compliance review is required.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workflows.
Confirm vendor DPAs and residency settings before use.
Keep secrets only in approved secret stores.
Document retention settings for both agents.
requires-engineering: perform a formal compliance assessment for the full data flow.
